notes.title: "Reignbreaker" Official Music Video by Djerv
notes.content:
The Official Music Video for Reignbreaker is Here!

The music video for "Reignbreaker," our game's title song by Norwegian metal band Djerv just dropped! Check it out on YouTube:

[previewyoutube=nqVUIUxCfnI;full][/previewyoutube]

A Creative and Fun Process from Start to Finish
“It was so much fun working with our friends again on this video. We wanted to create something that really captured the essence of Reignbreaker and its story, but also bring in a bit of humor. The whole process was creative and fun from start to finish — now we just hope people enjoy watching it as much as we enjoyed making it,” says vocalist Agnete Kjølsrud. The video was directed by Jørn Veberg and Dag Stian Mykjåland — a creative duo known for their visually striking and concept-driven productions.

“When you have a month with no clue what to do in the evenings — what do you do? You wait for a call from Djerv asking if you want to make a fully animated music video,” Veberg says with a grin.

Game Meets Music: A World in Rebellion
The video plunges us into a crumbling world ruled by a tyrannical queen whose reign is nearing its end. Reignbreaker and her ragtag crew rise up to claim the throne — all told through an aesthetic inspired by stylized, dystopian comic-book worlds. The result mirrors the raw intensity and energy ofthe track — with a sly wink along the way.

You can listen to "Reignbreaker" on streaming platforms, and play the game now on Steam! You can also purchase the soundtrack from our Steam page, which includes Djerv's explosive track. Check it out if you haven't yet, and follow us on social media to stay up-to date!

Photo: Jørn Veberg.

notes.title: "Reignbreaker" Official Song by Djerv - Streaming Now!
notes.content:
Djerv Returns with a Game-Changing Anthem for Reignbreaker

We've collaborated with Norwegian band Djerv to create the title track for our game: "Reignbreaker"! Listen to it now on streaming platforms, and check out the lyric video:

[previewyoutube=QqEXhsOiT94;full][/previewyoutube]

An Explosive Track for an Anti-Authoritarian Game
Djerv is known for blending intense rock, metal, and gaming culture in a way that has captured the attention of an international audience. With previous collaborations like "Get Jinxed" (League of Legends), "THE REDHOOD" (Nikke: Goddess of Victory), and "Rebel Heart" (Arcane: Season 2), they've made their mark on some of the world's most iconic games. This has led to nominations in 2025 for both the Norwegian Grammys in the "International Success of the Year" category and the Norwegian Music Publishing Awards in the "Sync of the Year" category.

Now they're taking it to the next level with "Reignbreaker," a track that combines metal, Agnete's iconic vocals, and driving rhythms with an uncompromising melody that mirrors the game's rebellious and anti-authoritarian theme.

“With this track, we wanted to try something new. It has a different vibe – almost like a march, something we've never done before. We've slowed down the tempo, but the energy is still intense,” says vocalist Agnete Kjølsrud. “It's about channeling the power and drive needed when you're ready to tear down the system.

A Perfect Match
Alexander "Pepe" Pieper, our studio head, describes why Djerv was the perfect band to create the track that would define the game: "Music has always been a big part of my identity, ever since I played in punk bands in the 2000s. When designing 'Reignbreaker,' we wanted it to feel like playing through an album like 'Battle of Los Angeles' by Rage Against the Machine — raw, rebellious, and full of energy. Punk isn't just about identity or graffiti; music is the core. Djerv was the perfect band to create a title track that captures that spirit. When we heard their work on League of Legends and Arcane, we knew they were the right choice, and they totally nailed it!”

Get Ready to Smash the Kingdom
Reignbreaker launches next week on March 18. You'll also be able to purchase the soundtrack on Steam, which includes Djerv's explosive new track "Reignbreaker." Play the demo to get a taste of our kingdom-smashing roguelike, and follow us on social media to stay up-to date!

Photo: Jørn Veberg.

notes.title: Dev Diary #5: Music & Audio
notes.content:
DEVSTREAM TODAY!
First things first: don’t miss our final pre-launch devstream TODAY, March 12, at 15:00 CET with one of our audio designers, who will be chatting about how his team crafted the unique medievalpunk soundscape of Reigbnreaker. Follow us on Twitch and don’t miss it!

WHAT DOES MEDIEVALPUNK SOUND LIKE?
Reignbreaker is medievalpunk game. Yes, we made up this word, but we like it because it captures the wild mashup of aesthetics and influences that feed into the game. That extends from the gameplay to the art to our focus today: sound design. "It was quite a process to find the right balance of punch, punk, and medieval soundscapes to represent the game’s anti-establishment direction,” says Markus Zierhofer of AudioCreatures, who created the audio for Reignbreaker. “Shaping the audio landscape, our entire team contributed to the audio direction, sound design, and music — destroying and recording countless guitars, and experimenting with various sounds through re-sampling and re-amping techniques to bring the world to life.”

AudioCreatures used both modern and medieval instruments to match the anachronistic influences of Reignbreaker, while also setting the mood: “We kept the music punchy while also adding melodic sequences in the combat music, which are tailored to match the enemies you’re fighting to create a cohesive and immersive game world”

https://i.imgur.com/WF8l1xE.gif
The Reignbreaker title track can be heard in the main menu — play the demo to listen now!

GETTING THE BAND TOGETHER
But the game still needed a punk rock anthem to get players in the mood to fight: “From the start, we really wanted to collaborate with an established punk band or artist,” says Markus, “and we were thrilled to arrange an extremely cool partnership for the game's title track. We're officially announcing and releasing the track onto streaming platforms on March 14 — but if you've played the demo and done some digging you probably who it is already. We're super pleased with the result, which is not only a perfect match for the game but also an absolute banger on its own!"

WEAPON SPOTLIGHT: BLAST
Finally, let's highlight the final and most chaotic Javelin bayonet in our series: the Blast Javelin. Basically, it makes your weapon explode on impact. This does a lot of damage to enemies, but it can damage you as well. Therefore it carries a very high risk of injury, but it’s (almost) always worth it.

Keep your distance while blasting enemy groups with the Throw:

https://i.imgur.com/2M7jvpV.gif
The Strike is a dive attack that plants a bomb, which goes off after a short time:

https://i.imgur.com/hm80M5H.gif
And the Slam explodes right where you're standing — so make sure to dash away ASAP:

https://i.imgur.com/cZ5sqaa.gif
LAUNCHING NEXT TUESDAY
Hey, so this is crazy, but we’re launching the game in less than a week. Please check out our demo if you haven’t yet, tell your friends, and tune in to our Twitch channel later today for our last pre-launch devstream!

xoxo
Studio Fizbin

notes.title: Dev Interview: The Art of Reignbreaker
notes.content:
As we gear up for the launch of Reignbreaker, the medievalpunk rogue-like, we caught up with Nadja Clauberg, the talented 2D artist responsible for some of the game’s most unforgettable character designs.

Nadja’s artistry has been crucial in defining the unique personalities and visual identities of the game’s characters, from their distinctive silhouettes to the intricate details that make them truly come alive.

In this interview, we dive into Nadja’s creative process, exploring her approach to character design, concept art, and how she ensured each character seamlessly fits into the world of Reignbreaker. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45157905/f290b4d5bd074f47d054ec5f5e20c13cfe043848.png
Q. Who are you and what is your role as part of the team behind Reignbreaker?

Hi, my name is Nadja and I am a 2D artist at Studio Fizbin. For Reignbreaker, one of my main responsibilities was designing and illustrating the character portraits in the game.

Q. What is your experience with concept art, and how does it differ from final asset creation?

At its core, concept art is a form of design. Designing — and therefore creating concept art — means visualizing ideas, which requires multiple iterations and discarding a fair share of them before moving forward. A functional concept art piece therefore doesn’t need to be highly rendered. Instead, its main purpose is to serve a specific function rather than just look pretty. I think that is a common misconception people tend to have. Especially looking at highly polished production art books can sometimes create a misleading or at least incomplete impression of what concept art is really about.

Q. Can you describe your artistic process when approaching designs for Reignbreaker?

The first phase of my concept art process is what I call the "Thinking Phase". Taking the time to properly think things through pays off later when creating final assets, because ideally, all major decisions have already been made. Now I can focus on making things look pretty.

When entering the Thinking Phase, I don’t start with sketches or drawing right away. Instead, I use mind maps and other creative thinking tools to generate ideas. Even though my work is mostly digital, I prefer doing this traditionally with a pencil and notebook.

Jumping straight into sketching and settling for the first idea that comes to mind can be risky, as it often leads to unoriginal ideas and the unconscious reproduction of stereotypes. That’s perfectly normal and just how our brains work! The key is to be aware of these traps and avoid falling into them.

Once the thinking process is done, I start gathering visual references and creating a moodboard. I try to limit references from existing media (like games, movies, or concept art) because they can make it too easy to repeat familiar ideas. Instead it’s useful to include a lot of real-world references as well, to ensure the designs feel authentic. That was especially important in a project like Reignbreaker, which is rooted in a historic medieval setting. Using reference from that time period, especially looking out for Gothic elements, makes the designs authentic and believable. For the punk elements, we tried looking into real designs of old school punk posters and generally references from the punk movement, including style elements and symbolism.

After the research phase, I start sketching, testing ideas, and sharing them with the team for feedback. This usually takes multiple iterations and refinements, which is a natural part of the process. During this phase, I avoid listening to music with lyrics or podcasts, as they can be distracting. Instead, I prefer instrumental music to help me focus.

Once a design is approved by the art director, all that’s left is creating the final asset or artwork: That means creating clean line art, painting, rendering and making everything visually polished. This phase requires less “thinking” and is more about technical skill, which is why I love listening to a good podcast or music with lyrics on the side.

Q. How did you ensure your art aligns with the overall vision and style of the game?

When I joined the team, there was already a strong artistic foundation, including detailed art pillars and a visual style guide, which helped me a lot in the beginning. I really enjoyed immersing myself in the world of Reignbreaker right from the start.

For the character portraits, we wanted to develop a unique art style that would make them memorable and recognizable while still fitting seamlessly into the game world. To achieve this, we experimented with different approaches for inking, coloring, and the balance between abstraction and stylization. Sometimes, this meant spending hours just testing digital inking brushes to find one that was both versatile and efficient for streamlined production! The game’s medieval punk setting with tech elements naturally allowed for unique designs, and I’m super happy with the results.

But good communication is a must, not just within the art department but across the entire team. Especially as a 2D and concept artist, you often rely on input from other departments, like game design or narrative, so avoiding misunderstandings through clear communication is key. After all, as a game artist, you’re visualizing the ideas of many people and bringing them to life.

Q. Do you have a favourite piece from the game? 

My favorite character to design and draw was Ardea, the Spearsister. I’m always happy to encounter her in a run, not only because she grants some of my favorite skills, but also because she has an especially compelling backstory.

She shares a past in the Queen’s regiment with our main character, Clef, who later became a rebel. Now that they’re on opposite sides, their relationship is complex and layered, which makes their interactions in the game fascinating to witness.

Q. Is there anything you think players should look out for - any hidden easter eggs? 

When you come back to the lobby after every run, please say hello to Baby Bellgrunt, cause he is adorable and deserves every fist bump he can get. 

Q. What do you hope players will take away from Reignbreaker? 

I hope Reignbreaker helps players appreciate the value of a diverse character cast and visual representation beyond traditional gender stereotypes, not just in our game but in all forms of media.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45157905/849a6e45cb6f9a5a086b76715491473501f61e93.png

Reignbreaker will be launching on Steam on March 18th, but you can play the demo now. 

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2129810/Reignbreaker/

notes.title: Dev Diary #4: Progression & Advanced Tactics
notes.content:
DEVSTREAM TODAY!
But first: just like every week, we'll be streaming TODAY, March 5, at 15:00 CET with our lead game designer to get into the nitty-gritty details of the game. Follow us on Twitch and tune in!

FIGHTING FOR PROGRESS
So what does character progression look like in Reignbreaker? You'll get KO'd a lot in this game, but that's just a small setback: all of your progress is saved from run to run...except your Key Money, which the Trench Rats will happily take as their "fee" for rescuing you from death. Most importantly, you'll still have your Resolve: strange crystals that hold a powerful energy. You can spend Resolve in camp for permanent character upgrades like increased health, additional moves, new punch combos, resurrections, better or different Vault items, and more.

https://i.imgur.com/YCHQ6xO.gif
AN ARSENAL FOR THE AGES
There are dozens of Javelins to collect over the course of your campaign, so by the end you'll have amassed quite the arsenal of weapons to maximize your reignbreaking abilities. Want a Javelin that adds a damage-over-time debuff? How about one that attaches a sticky bomb to enemies? Some Javelins trigger after a couple seconds, letting you steer clear of the explosion. A few even act like proximity mines, triggering only when an enemy gets close.

https://i.imgur.com/cdKH1SC.gif
You'll start with just one simple Javelin, but will soon unlock more by quickly completing chambers, reaching certain points in the campaign, or just by finding them hidden away in the dark corners of the Bastion. Keep your eyes peeled!

DIFFICULTY SPIKES
Unlike many other games in the roguelike genre, Reignbreaker follows a campaign structure that gradually ramps up in difficulty over time. Your first raid will be a fairly simple affair, with smaller waves, weaker enemies, and a miniboss encounter at the end. But if you can defeat the Guardian in the final room, the Bastion's chambers will shift -- meaning your next raid attempt won't be so easy. The Queen will throw even more types of enemies at you, they'll be harder to kill, and they might even have new abilities or resistances. But that's nothing you can't handle, right?

WEAPON SPOTLIGHT: TORNADO
This Javelin will literally blow you away. (sorry) The Tornado bayonet gives you more control of the battlefield by letting you push enemies around. It may do less damage, but clever players will find ways to use the environment to their advantage, and combine these attacks with other Javelins to create devastating new playstyles.

The Strike pushes enemies back – perfect for launching them into traps:

https://i.imgur.com/ccGBT5k.gif
The Slam creates a long-lasting whirlwind that sucks up nearby enemies:

https://i.imgur.com/blgKcF8.gif
And the Throw creates a whirlwind on whichever enemy it lands on: 

https://i.imgur.com/Ycd1hYT.gif
DEMO NEWS
We’ve been super happy with the response you all had to the Steam Next Fest demo, so we’ve decided to leave it up! Please check it out if you haven’t already, and if you have, please leave a review to let us know what you think! Finally, remember to follow us on Twitch to catch our livestream today, and next week our FINAL livestream before launch!

xoxo

Studio Fizbin

notes.title: Dev Diary #3: The Art of Reignbreaker
notes.content:
BEHIND-THE-SCENES ARTIST STREAM TOMORROW!
Before we get into it: two of our artists will be on the stream tomorrow, Feb 26, at 15:00 CET to show how they designed the unique medievalpunk world of Reignbreaker. Follow us on Twitch to and tune in for an in-depth look at how game art is created!

KITBASHING A MEDIEVALPUNK WORLD

The world of Reignbreaker was conceptualized as a dark fantasy reflection of our own. As we were trying to grapple with the continued rise of right wing authoritarian governments across the world, we imagined what it would be like if a medieval monarch had somehow acquired a means to cement their absolute authority. And what would the resistance look like? This resulted in a mash-up aesthetic that we eventually called “medievalpunk” – blending elements from typical medieval fantasy with sci-fi technology, alongside a rebellion that sports a more modern & anachronistic punk style.

Our design was also inspired by kitbashing – a term from modelmaking that means taking model parts from different kits and “bashing” them together to make original creations. We thought would be a perfect fit for our brand of high-tech feudalism (and also because a lot of people in our studio are miniature wargame nerds). We imagined the blacksmiths and engineers of this world would take medieval objects and "bash" them with sci fi technologies to create new machines and animated guardians. You can see this in your main weapon – a medieval lance slapped with a bunch of high-tech bells and whistles – or our enemy designs, which incorporate objects like church bells, statues, and medieval weaponry:

https://i.imgur.com/MNxbPiI.png

BETWEEN 2D AND 3D
For the environments of Reignbreaker we landed on a “2.5D” art style, combining 2D and 3D objects for a style that fuses the best of both worlds, and utilizes the wide-ranging specialties of our art team. The end product marries the handcrafted look of a 2D game with the functionality of 3D environments and objects. By going into the game engine and move the camera to different angles, you can see how each environment is a mix of flat objects and three-dimensional objects:

https://i.imgur.com/xVkHI0D.gif

WEAPON SPOTLIGHT: SHOTGUN
Everyone knows what a shotgun does. But what happens when you strap one to a medievalpunk Javelin? Well, we imagined you’d get a powerful close-range weapon that’s as deadly as it is satisfying. Like all Javelin types, it can be deployed in three ways:

The Strike is a point-blank blast to the face to any enemies in your way, which can be chained together into a sick three-part combo:

https://i.imgur.com/Q4pM0iw.gif
The Throw gets lodged in an enemy’s face and blasts anything behind it:

https://i.imgur.com/tYGdzPF.gif
And the Slam creates a short-lived but intense turret:

https://i.imgur.com/UgcLTsr.gif
The demo for Reignbreaker is available throughout Steam Next Fest, so check it out while you can, and if you’ve already played, please leave a review – it helps us reach many more players! Remember to follow us on Twitch to catch our next devstream, and we’ll be back again with another blog next week.

xoxo
Studio Fizbin

notes.title: Dev Diary #2: Combat
notes.content:
Hey Reignbreakers, we’re back at it with a deep dive into combat!

DEV STREAM TOMORROW!
We’re going live on Twitch at 15:00 CET tomorrow, Feb 19, to show off the finer points of Reignbreaker’s combat system. Follow us on Twitch to see the game in action and ask us your questions live!

FIGHTING 101
Here’s a quick rundown on how to beat the Queen’s machines. As a Battlefield Machinist, your primary weapon is a mighty Javelin, which can do three kinds of attacks: an aimed Throw that hits a single enemy at range, a Slam that damages enemies around you in a small radius, and a melee Strike that hits enemies in front of you in close-to-medium range. These attacks always do some damage on impact, and also shoot projectiles depending on which Bayonet is equipped. 

Your Javelin attacks are limited by Heat – use too many attacks too quickly and your Javelin will overheat, forcing you to wait until it cools down again.

Punches are close-range attacks that are especially useful because they don’t add heat and even help decrease your heat gauge faster. Keeping a balance between punches and Javelin attacks is a good way to keep you in the flow of combat and rack up a high combo level.

Speaking of the Combo Level – you can build it up by performing lots of attacks in close succession. The higher your combo level, the more Keys you earn to spend on upgrades. Certain Vault Items also increase your damage or give you other bonuses based on your level, so keep that combo going!

Finally, certain enemies need to be Executed when knocked out, or else they’ll get back up. Go finish them off before they get the chance – and enjoy a massive heat reduction while doing so.

https://i.imgur.com/faDG9QO.gif
WEAPON SPOTLIGHT: RAILGUN
Ever wanted to rain down hellfire on your enemies? Well, the Railgun comes pretty close. As one of the five primary weapon variants, the Railgun is a heavy projectile that’s as destructive as it is cool-looking:

The Strike is a large sweeping attack perfect for clearing out groups of enemies:

https://i.imgur.com/NKJmAg2.gif
The Throw ricochets and hits another enemy:

https://i.imgur.com/qsPrSFr.gif
And the Slam rains down a barrage of heavy fire – after a quick delay, so time it carefully:

https://i.imgur.com/4lzTts6.gif
SWAPPING WEAPONS
Early in the game you’ll unlock the ability to carry not one, but two Javelins with you into each run, which you can swap between at any time. This provides a lot of flexibility in choosing which weapons you’d like to bring into combat. Some Javelins have more specific use cases, so bringing along a complementary weapon ensures you’ll be ready for whatever the Bastion throws at you.


GET THE GUARDIANS
The first major boss you’ll meet in the game is the Chimera – a nasty piece of work that will put your combat skills to the test. Don’t expect your first encounter to go well.

https://i.imgur.com/YgxsvE4.gif
We’ll be attempting to kill the Chimera ourselves tomorrow on Twitch at 15:00 CET!

Thanks for reading, and we’ll be back next week for a closer look at the art and visual effects of Reignbreaker. See you there!

– Studio Fizbin

notes.title: Dev Diary #1: Meet Clef
notes.content:
Hey Reignbreakers, we’re kicking off a series of dev diaries this week to give you a behind-the-scenes look at development, what you can expect from the game, and why we’re making it! But first:

DEV STREAM
We’re going to go into all of this in much more depth in a series of livestreams over the next few weeks. Check out the stream on our Twitch channel on Wednesday, February 12 from 15:00-17:00 CET! Follow us on Twitch and turn on notifications to ask us your questions live!

Let’s get to it:

RAIDING THE BASTION
The queen has erected a technologically advanced stronghold to cement her absolute power: the Bastion. Everything inside is carefully guarded by animated machines and secured behind strong locks – luckily, you’ve got a big key.

You are Clef – a woman who grew up as a child conscript in the Queen’s private regiment, where you learned to wield their signature weapon: the Javelin. Equal parts weapon and lockpick, Javelins can beat down enemies as easily as they can break into Vaults.

WEAPON SPOTLIGHT: PEASHOOTER
Your Javelin always comes equipped with one of five different Bayonets, which determine what projectiles it shoots. The Peashooter is the first Bayonet type you’ll encounter in the game. But don’t let its humble name fool you – this Javelin can pack a powerful punch, shooting out a barrage of small bullets to chip away at enemies' health. Like all the Bayonets in Reignbreaker, the Peashooters have three different attack styles:

The Slam creates a mini turret that shoots bullets in many different directions:

https://i.imgur.com/5EUOhou.gif
The Strike shoots a barrage of bullets directly in front of you:

https://i.imgur.com/FkNP2ay.gif

And the Throw lodges the Javelin right into the enemy's body and starts firing – gunning down the enemy and anything behind it:

https://i.imgur.com/ne03mFb.gif
POWER UP
This is a roguelike, so of course there are powerups you collect in each run to get stronger and encourage you to try out different combat styles. Inside the Bastion you’ll go from Vault to Vault. When you try to crack it, it triggers a combat lockdown that you must defeat in order to proceed. Each Vault is under the protection of one of the four Loyalists…more on them in a future blog!

https://i.imgur.com/HcEwy8U.gif

ORIGIN OF THE GAME
Studio Fizbin has been around since 2011! We got our start making VERY different games from Reignbreaker: you might know us from our point-and-click adventure series The Inner World, or our puzzle platformer Minute of Islands, or our one-button-game Say NO! More. All of these games had a heavy focus on unique art styles and compelling worlds that tell socially-relevant stories. But after our last couple games, we wanted to expand and make our biggest game yet, and create something that had deeper and more engaging gameplay, while retaining the special sauce that made all our previous games feel Fizbin-y.

https://i.imgur.com/tScJqiZ.gif

As we recently said in our dev diary trailer, Reignbreaker came about as a response to the resurgence of right-wing authoritarianism in many places around the world. This makes a lot of people feel scared or helpless, so we wanted to create a power fantasy game where players could fight back, stepping into the boots of an anarchist punk rebel, using their controllers to smash apart a brutal and oppressive regime. Hell yeah.

So if you want to know more, tune in to the livestream on 12 Feb from 15:00-17:00 CET, or write your questions on this post and we’ll answer them live!

Next week we’ll take a deeper dive into combat. Follow us on social media to catch all the latest Reignbreaker news, and see ya next time!

– Studio Fizbin
